title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: on the previous pages Grothendieck defined a 'Teichmüller–Galois' category attached to a base field k (an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0). Its connected objects, up to isomorphism, correspond one-to-one with the numerical types (g,ν) of algebraic curves. The automorphism groups of its objects are (up to inner automorphisms) the profinite completions of the Teichmüller (mapping-class) groups. Its morphisms come from finite étale coverings between curves, together with Galois descent. The previous page also says it is equivalent to a category of algebraic curves.

This page draws the moral of that construction.

(1) The underlying object is the 'Teichmüller–Poincaré groupoid': the fundamental groupoid of the moduli stacks M_{g,ν}, taken over all types (g,ν). Enlarging this groupoid to a genuine category, no longer a groupoid, is the natural way to relate curves of different numerical types (g,ν). A covering Y→X of a curve of type (g,ν) by a curve of type (g',ν') induces, after passing to a level structure / finite cover of the moduli stack, a morphism of moduli stacks M_{g,ν}[Γ] → M_{g',ν'}. On fundamental groupoids this gives non-invertible arrows linking different mapping-class groups. Each finite-index subgroup of π_1 of the surface, invariant under a finite-index subgroup of the mapping-class group, yields a homomorphism from that subgroup to the mapping-class group of the covering surface.

(2) Programme. An essential part of his 'programme à l'horizon' is to determine this category, together with the operations on it, 'more or less completely' and 'by algebraic means'. The inserted parenthesis specifies: neither transcendental (no complex-analytic Teichmüller theory) nor by algebraic geometry. The margin explains that 'algebraic' should mean a presentation of generators-and-relations type, built on the combinatorics of maps (cartes / dessins) and of the relevant multiplicities. This is the combinatorial approach later pursued for the Teichmüller tower and GT.

(3) Scope. This is to be done at least for k = Q̄ (where the category carries the Gal(Q̄/Q)-action). To some extent it should also be done for k = K̄ with K finitely generated over Q, possibly restricting to curves defined over K (the end of the sentence is unclear).

The next page notes that one further type of morphism is still missing: open immersions X = Y∖T ↪ Y ('bouchage des trous', filling in punctures). Admitting them forces one to consider diagrams with X̂ → Ŷ finite and X → Y étale. Thus the category is being built toward something like 'the category of hyperbolic curves with finite étale maps and puncture-fillings', seen through profinite fundamental groupoids.
errors: No mathematical error; the page is programmatic.

Gap: the exact definition of morphisms, i.e. which coverings induce which maps of moduli stacks, depends on the preceding pages and is not restated. The final clause about K̄ versus K-curves is left unfinished ('qui sont des K-courbes .... Q?').
As the next page admits, the category as defined here omits open immersions (filling punctures). So it does not yet 'relate all types' compatibly with the Knudsen-style forgetful maps.

ideas.what: Profinite fundamental groupoid of the moduli stacks M_{g,ν} (all types) as the basic object carrying the Gal(Q̄/Q)-action
ideas.modern_name: Teichmüller tower / profinite mapping-class groupoid; outer Galois representation on π_1(M_{g,n})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984); developed by Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps

ideas.what: Enlarging the Teichmüller groupoid to a non-groupoid category whose arrows come from finite coverings between curves of different types (g,ν)→(g',ν'), inducing maps between finite covers of moduli stacks / mapping-class groups
ideas.modern_name: Morphisms of moduli stacks induced by characteristic covers; 'Teichmüller–Galois category'; related to the category of hyperbolic (orbi)curves with finite étale maps in anabelian geometry
ideas.usually_credited_to: Covering-induced maps between mapping-class groups: Birman–Hilden, Looijenga, Boggi (congruence subgroup problem), Asada. Categorical anabelian versions: Mochizuki, Hoshi–Mochizuki
ideas.where_published: The Esquisse stresses the tower with gluing/cutting operations rather than covering morphisms; this explicit non-groupoid 'Teichmüller–Galois category' does not appear there in this form

ideas.what: Programme of describing this category purely 'algebraically': generators and relations via combinatorics of maps/dessins, avoiding both transcendental and algebro-geometric methods
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial / generators-and-relations presentation of the Teichmüller tower; GT-type descriptions; dessins d'enfants
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (generators-and-relations description of the Teichmüller tower; dessins)

ideas.what: Extension of the programme from Q̄ to K̄ with K finitely generated over Q
ideas.modern_name: Galois action of finitely generated fields on profinite mapping-class groups; anabelian geometry over finitely generated fields
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983), in the context of anabelian conjectures over finitely generated fields

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly considers a category, not a groupoid, linking the profinite Teichmüller groups of all types (g,ν) via covering-induced morphisms. On the next page he adds open immersions (puncture-filling). He proposes to determine it, with its Galois action, combinatorially. This merges two strands kept separate in the later literature. One is the Teichmüller tower and GT, which uses gluing and forgetful operations. The other is the covering-map functoriality between different mapping-class groups (used in the congruence subgroup problem by Boggi and Asada), and the categories of hyperbolic curves in Mochizuki-style anabelian geometry. GT-type actions compatible with all covering morphisms between different types are little studied.
missed.quote: Le fait d'avoir élargi le groupoïde des Teichmüller–Poincaré en la catégorie (qui n'est plus un groupoïde !) des Teichmüller–Galois précédente, est une façon naturelle pour relier entre eux des courbes alg. relatives à des types numériques (g,ν) différents.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This suggests an enlarged Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group: the automorphisms of the full Teichmüller–Galois category, including covering morphisms. One can ask whether it coincides with GT-hat or with the image of Gal(Q̄/Q). That question touches current work on GT versus Gal(Q̄/Q) and on the congruence subgroup property.

missed.claim: The programme to determine this category 'by algebraic means', i.e. generators and relations through the combinatorics of maps, was left at the level of intention. Treatments for K̄ with K finitely generated, and for the version enlarged by puncture-filling morphisms, do not appear in the literature.
missed.quote: Une part essentielle du ... 'programme à l'horizon' est de déterminer de façon plus ou moins complète cette catégorie par voie 'algébrique' (ni transcendante ni de géométrie algébrique !)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: No combinatorial presentation of the covering morphisms between profinite mapping-class groups is known. A presentation would bear on GT, on congruence-subgroup questions and on dessins.

deep.surprise_reason: The overall programme (combinatorial determination of the Teichmüller tower with its Galois action) is well known from the Esquisse. What is less known is the explicit non-groupoid 'Teichmüller–Galois' category, built from covering morphisms between different types (and, next page, open immersions), which predates the Esquisse's gluing-based formulation. It is a notable unpublished variant but not a finished result.
